speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To begin, can you describe exactly how your gait and limb coordination have changed, and when did these symptoms first appear?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any history of alcohol abuse, vitamin B12 deficiency, or exposure to heavy metals like lead or mercury? I also need to know if you’ve experienced any recent head trauma or infections.

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of Crohn's disease and natalizumab use, I am concerned about Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML). REQUEST TEST: Brain MRI with contrast.

speaker: Doctor
text: REQUEST TEST: JC Virus PCR in cerebrospinal fluid.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the JC Virus PCR is negative, PML is effectively ruled out. Given your right-sided asymmetry and Crohn's history, I need to check for other causes of neurologic deficits. REQUEST TEST: Vitamin B12 and Folate levels.

speaker: Doctor
text: With PML and B12 deficiency ruled out, I suspect natalizumab-induced immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome or an inflammatory demyelinating process. REQUEST TEST: CSF analysis for oligoclonal bands and cell count.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the CSF analysis is normal, I need to rule out structural causes like a tumor or stroke. REQUEST TEST: Brain CT scan.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since structural and common inflammatory causes are ruled out, I need to assess for cerebellar toxicity or paraneoplastic syndromes. Do you experience any visual changes, such as double vision or loss of peripheral vision, and have you noticed any recent weight loss or night sweats?

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had a recent fever or major infection that I know of. The symptoms are mostly gait imbalance, limb ataxia, and weaker use of my right arm.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the right-sided weakness and ataxia with negative inflammatory and infectious workups, I need to rule out a vascular event. REQUEST TEST: MRA of head and neck.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Cerebellar Ataxia secondary to Natalizumab therapy
